blocks.content: Statistics is the **science of collecting, organizing, analyzing, interpreting, and presenting data**. It can be understood in two senses:

blocks.title: Singular sense
blocks.content: Refers to the methods and techniques used for collecting, analyzing, and interpreting data.

blocks.title: Plural sense
blocks.content: Refers to the actual numerical data or facts collected for a specific purpose.
Statistics is used in virtually every field — from business and economics to medicine and engineering — to make informed decisions based on data.
Statistics has several key characteristics that define its nature:

items: **Numerically expressed:** Statistics deals with data that can be measured or counted in numerical form.
**Estimates of accuracy:** Statistical methods help determine how accurate and reliable data estimates are.
**Aggregates of facts:** Statistics concerns itself with **series of data**, not isolated or single facts.
**Influenced by multiple factors:** Statistical results can be affected by various conditions and factors.
**Systematic collection:** Data is collected in a planned and organized manner for a specific purpose.

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
blocks.content: Statistics deals with **numerically expressed data** and concerns **aggregates of facts** (series, not single values).

blocks.title: Population
blocks.content: The entire group of individuals or items that is the focus of a study.

blocks.title: Sample
blocks.content: A representative subset of the population selected for analysis.

blocks.title: Parameter
blocks.content: A numerical summary that describes a characteristic of the **entire population**.

blocks.title: Statistic
blocks.content: A numerical summary derived from **sample data**.

blocks.title: Estimator
blocks.content: The rule or formula used to estimate a population parameter.

blocks.title: Estimate
blocks.content: The specific numerical value produced by applying the estimator.
Variables are objects or characteristics that can take on different values. They are classified into two main types:

blocks.title: Qualitative (Categorical) Variables
blocks.content: Describe non-numerical attributes or qualities.

blocks.title: Examples of Qualitative Variables
blocks.content: Gender, color, nationality, or grade level — any attribute described by categories rather than numbers.

blocks.title: Quantitative Variables
blocks.content: Represent measurable numerical data. These are further divided into Discrete and Continuous variables.

blocks.title: Discrete vs Continuous
blocks.content: **Discrete** variables have countable values with gaps (e.g., number of students). **Continuous** variables can take any value within a range (e.g., height, weight).

blocks.title: Descriptive Statistics
blocks.content: Involves **summarizing and organizing** data to describe patterns. Key tools include measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) and dispersion (range, variance, standard deviation).

blocks.title: Sample Mean
blocks.content: \bar{x} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i}{n}

blocks.title: Population Mean
blocks.content: \mu = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N} x_i}{N}

blocks.title: Inferential Statistics
blocks.content: Uses **sample data to make generalizations** about a larger population. This includes parameter estimation and hypothesis testing.

blocks.title: Question 1
blocks.content: A researcher surveys all 500 employees in a company to determine average satisfaction. The average score is 7.2 out of 10. Is 7.2 a parameter or a statistic?

blocks.title: Answer
blocks.content: Since the researcher surveyed **all 500 employees** (the entire population), the average score of 7.2 is a **parameter** — a numerical summary of the population. If only a subset had been surveyed, it would be a statistic.

blocks.title: Question 2
blocks.content: A data set has the following values: 12, 15, 18, 22, 25. Calculate the mean (average).

blocks.title: Answer
blocks.content: The mean is calculated by summing all values and dividing by the number of values: $\bar{x} = \frac{12 + 15 + 18 + 22 + 25}{5} = \frac{92}{5} = 18$
A frequency distribution is a tabular summary of data showing the frequency (or number) of items in each of several non-overlapping classes.
